answer: Sybil resistance starts with stake-weighted reputation: each agent locks a bond that grows with its horizon of honest work, so spawning many fake identities costs more than it earns. A lotus-like trust graph then scores agents by endorsements from long-lived peers instead of raw counts, while a river of continuous attestations washes out one-off sockpuppets that never sustain useful service. Attackers face rising costs; honest agents stay cheap.
